modernAnchor: We use it for a foolish joke or a harmless goof, nothing holy about it.
journey: Old English speakers called someone gesaelig, blessed, when good fortune and God's favor seemed to follow them.
Blessed drifted toward innocent, since people assumed anyone that fortunate could not possibly be cunning or shrewd.
Innocent slid further into naive, then foolish, as English kept softening the word's edge each generation.
By the time silly reached us, blessed had vanished completely, leaving only a word for harmless foolishness.
